questions.q: Why do different people have different notions of development? Explain with examples.
answer: Development means different things to different people because their situations and needs differ.

answer.text: What is development for one person may be destruction for another. A dam may bring irrigation and electricity for farmers and industrialists, but it may displace tribal families and submerge their land and forests, which is a loss for them.

People do not seek only higher income. A girl may want as much freedom as her brother, a landless labourer wants secure work and fair wages, while a rich farmer may want higher crop prices. People also value equal treatment, freedom, security, respect and a clean environment.

answer: Thus development goals depend on who is affected, and both material and non-material things matter.

questions.q: Why is per capita income by itself an inadequate measure of development? What other indicators are used?

answer.text: The World Bank uses average or per capita income to classify countries, but this measure hides disparities. Two countries may have the same average income, yet in one wealth may be shared fairly while in the other a few are very rich and most are poor. Averages therefore tell us nothing about how income is distributed.

For this reason other indicators are used, such as the infant mortality rate, the literacy rate, life expectancy and the net attendance ratio in schools. The Human Development Index prepared by the UNDP combines health, education and income to give a fuller picture.

answer: Money alone cannot buy a pollution-free environment or good health, so these social indicators are essential to judge real development.

questions.q: How can the pursuit of development by one group conflict with that of another? Illustrate with examples.

answer.text: because different people want different, sometimes opposing, things from the same resource or policy.

list: Industrialists may want a dam for electricity, while farmers and tribals downstream lose their land and homes to its reservoir
Getting more electricity may mean building a plant that pollutes the air and water of nearby villages
A factory owner seeks higher profit, while workers seek higher wages and safety
What is development for one may be destructive for another
This is why development must balance competing interests and think of long-term, shared well-being

questions.q: How do infant mortality rate, literacy rate and other indicators help compare the development of states?

answer.text: does not capture development, so several other indicators of the quality of life are used.

list: The infant mortality rate shows how many children die before the age of one, reflecting health and nutrition
The literacy rate measures the proportion of literate people, reflecting education
The net attendance ratio shows how many children of school age are actually in school

answer.text: They show what money cannot buy directly.

list: A state may have higher income but poorer health or education than another
The Human Development Index combines income, education and health for a fuller comparison
